target_customer: Developers: first AWS serverless teams using SST, now individual developers and teams using an open source AI coding agent
problem: At YC, building serverless applications on AWS was hard to set up and test. The company later moved to open source AI coding agents that work with any model provider.
business_model: open source with paid subscriptions and console (OpenCode Go from 10 USD per month, low cost model subscriptions, team tools); earlier SST Console from 20 USD per month per workspace
product_category: developer tools, serverless framework then AI coding agent

founders.name: Jay V
founders.background_notes: YC page: founder at Anomaly. Company blog (July 2021) announced the seed round; TechCrunch says Jay V and Frank Wang founded Serverless Stack in 2017.

technical_complexity.rationale: SST v2 built on AWS CDK with live debugging. The later coding agent is a large open source terminal and desktop product that integrates 200 plus providers; moderately hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code can be forked, as the OpenCode name dispute shows. Community size and the Models.dev database give distribution rather than a technical moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As an AI agent OpenCode competes with Claude Code and Codex. Anthropic restricted use of Claude subscriptions through OpenCode in 2026 per press, which boosted its growth rather than hurting it.

market_need_then: SST's own guide (Serverless Framework vs SST) says developers found Serverless Framework painful, and the 2021 seed announcement states demand for easier serverless apps. Dated 2021 competitor pages were not retrieved.

branding.name_origin: SST was formerly Serverless Stack and shortened because the old name was long and easily confused with Serverless Framework (SST docs). OpenCode name origin not found.
branding.domain_note: Moved from serverless-stack.com to sst.dev; opencode.ai for the agent.

identity.logo: OpenCode has a brand page and custom font; details not retrieved
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and concise, focused on openness and user choice (site, 2026).

branding.brand_signature: Open source coding agent that works with any model

rebrands.why: Old name was long and easy to confuse with Serverless Framework

branding.community_and_virality: Hacker News front page threads, 1,000 plus contributors listed on the site and reports of 150,000 plus GitHub stars from secondary sources. A separate earlier OpenCode project by another developer caused a naming dispute per a Hacker News thread (unverified).

brand_strength.rationale: OpenCode gained wide mindshare among developers in 2025 and 2026 per press, though the name is generic and was disputed.

pivots.to: OpenCode open source AI coding agent
pivots.why: Not stated in the sources opened; the same team (Anomaly) built both and the YC listing now shows OpenCode.

outcome_analysis: The YC W21 company was Serverless Stack (SST), an open source AWS framework that raised a 1M seed from Greylock, SV Angel and YC in July 2021. The same team later built OpenCode, an open source coding agent that press reports at over 13 million monthly users. Press attributes part of the growth to Anthropic limiting subscription use. A security incident and free usage controversy are reported. Later funding was not found, so the company may be bootstrapped or undisclosed.
notes: The directory slug and name say OpenCode but the YC W21 batch was Serverless Stack, now Anomaly. The YC page says Toronto and founded 2010, which conflicts with TechCrunch (founded 2017, San Francisco), so founded_year uses 2017. Third co-founders Dax Raad and Adam Elmore appear only in secondary reports, so are not listed as founders. CB Insights shows 1.67M over 3 rounds for Anomaly (aggregator, unverified). Some reports mention an undisclosed round for OpenCode; not recorded. Competitor search retrieved only SST authored and 2026 comparison pages, none dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Founder education and prior employers not found.
